statements.quote: But we should not be blind to the fact there are some downside risks, you know, bio-terrorism, other things that we need to be very concerned about.

statements.venue: Fox News interview with Harris Faulkner (transcript in Senate press release)
statements.quote: All these predictions never came true. I hear a little bit of that right now from some of my colleagues on the left side of the aisle who are creating hysteria and want to create this to be a political issue versus thoughtfulness here in Washington
statements.context: Discussing the AI debate in Washington, he compared current warnings from Democratic colleagues to past 'climate change hysteria' that 'the world was going to end'.

statements.quote: We cannot go down the left’s call to stop or put a moratorium in AI. That hands this race right to China.
statements.context: Closing his argument for light-touch 'appropriate guardrails' rather than halting AI development.
statements.reason: Opposes a stop or moratorium on AI on competition grounds; no catastrophic risk is acknowledged in this passage.

statements.venue: Fox News interview with Harris Faulkner (transcript in Senate press release)
statements.quote: The recursive nature of AI, what that means is AI is now programming AI. It’s becoming less about humans generating the next frontier models as AI generating the next AI models.
statements.context: Explaining why AI is moving too fast for Washington to keep up, before asking how to set guardrails that protect the public without inhibiting innovation.
statements.reason: Describes AI building the next AI models as a matter of speed and mentions 'possible downsides' and guardrails, but states no consequence or catastrophic harm.

record: Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 Senate Democrats urging AI talks with China (not on the verified signer list).
Said in Fox News and Fox Business interviews that the US must not slow down or put a moratorium on AI, and called for light 'adaptive governance' with 'appropriate guardrails'.
Told Semafor, on federal action over state AI laws, that he would 'rather see Congress sort this out'.
grade_reason: His one acknowledgment of catastrophic risk is a brief mention of bioterrorism as an AI downside 'we need to be very concerned about' (B, borderline C). In the same interview he compared colleagues' AI warnings to climate 'hysteria' whose predictions 'never came true' (F, uncertain); under the brief's rule the B outranks the F, but a reviewer should weigh both.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. All four Daines press release pages (15 Sept, 16 Sept, 23 Sept, 1 Oct 2026) were downloaded and every quote was checked by script to be an exact continuous passage of the page text; the quotes are from the office's own transcripts of TV interviews, not checked against the video. The transcripts omit the host's questions and use ellipses between passages, so the F statement's target (which warnings he called hysteria) is inferred: the section is headed 'Daines on the AI race versus China' and follows mid-September 2026 news of AI researchers' extinction warnings. The full sentence before the F quote, cut for the 300-character limit, is: 'It reminds me a bit, Harris, remember the days of the climate change hysteria coming from the left about the world was going to end, the polar ice caps were going to be gone and so forth.' Also in the 15 Sept interview, not quoted as a statement: a hypothetical about a news article on 'how your company destroyed part of this economy or humanity because of your technology', used to argue that companies police themselves. The 1 Oct 2026 Nixon Foundation remarks mention AI only as adoption and competition with China (D, not included). The Semafor article (9 Dec 2025) was read through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording ('We've got senators for sure who have very thoughtful views on both sides of the issue. I'd rather see Congress sort this out.') is not verified character for character and is left out of statements; it concerns state versus federal AI rules (D). Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing Daines as a co-sponsor; Congress.gov was not checked, and the search results on its co-sponsor list conflicted with each other. No statements by him found on superintelligence, extinction or a China AI agreement. News coverage of his 2026 China trips (SCMP and others) was seen only in search results and not opened.
